title: Making health data ready for research
summary: Building transparent medication-processing workflows, with traceability from survey responses to research-ready data.
question: How can we make medication data consistent and reusable without losing what the original responses mean?
body: Reliable analysis starts with reliable data. My work on medication data processing uses explicit source specifications, harmonisation rules, validation and medication mapping to make each transformation inspectable.

The GLAD medication pilot provides a starting point for workflows that can support related cohorts and surveys. A central concern is preserving source identity, missing-value meanings and questionnaire context.
approach: Validate incoming data against a documented source specification.
Apply consistent processing and mapping rules with explicit provenance.
Produce quality-control reports that support review and reuse.
perspective: A research-ready dataset needs more than a clean table: it needs a record of what changed, why it changed and which uncertainties remain.
